world_org_meetings.title: Iran must stop arming Houthis in Yemen, G7 says ahead of UN General Assembly
world_org_meetings.description: The G7 also condemns "in the strongest terms" Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, saying that the escalation in fighting in Yemen jeopardises global energy security.

world_org_meetings.title: Watch: Threats, deals and passionate speeches at UNGA event
world_org_meetings.description: Delegations from across the world attended the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

world_org_meetings.title: The United Nations General Assembly is meeting. Is it accomplishing anything?
world_org_meetings.description: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with Michael Froman, Council on Foreign Relations president, at the UN General Assembly.

world_org_meetings.title: Macron urges world to 'stand firm' against 'abuse of power by empires' in final UN speech
world_org_meetings.description: French President Emmanuel Macron used his last address before the UN General Assembly as France's leader to urge the world's nations to stand alongside the United Nations in the face of a resurgent "law of the jungle". Macron also called for a moratorium on strikes on civilian and energy infrastructure in the Russia-Ukraine war and an "open-source" model for frontier AI independent of China and the US.

world_org_meetings.title: Trump's world? Leaders navigate consequences of US policy
world_org_meetings.description: A year ago, Donald Trump went to the rostrum of the United Nations General Assembly - and after taxing an axe to US aid and development funding, read the world the riot act. One Iran war later, the US president sticking to script with a speech that borrowed much of the language of last year. With citizens on five continents now feeling the pain at the pump, we'll ask what it will take to tame a global energy crisis whose potential spiral mirrors the contagion of hostilities from the Strait of Hormuz to the mouth of the Red Sea?

diplomatic_visits.title: Modi to visit Canada as Carney looks to finalize trade deal with India by end of year
diplomatic_visits.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to visit Canada in December, Prime Minister Mark Carney confirmed on Tuesday, as the two countries look to reach a trade deal by the end of the year — further signs that the once deep diplomatic chasm between the two governments is being bridged.

diplomatic_visits.title: 'What he's doing is positively un-American': Late-night hosts react to Trump media ban
diplomatic_visits.description: The comedians of late-night television have a vested interest in protecting the First Amendment. So when U.S. President Donald Trump announced he was banning news outlets CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House last Friday, they came out swinging.

diplomatic_visits.title: As Trump-Xi summit nears, Europe is caught in middle of US-China rivalry
diplomatic_visits.description: China's Xi Jinping is traveling to Washington this week. Regardless of what comes from his talks with US President Trump, the EU will likely remain stuck between erratic US trade policy and Beijing's export machine.

diplomatic_visits.title: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian arrives in New York for UNGA
diplomatic_visits.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has arrived in New York as the US-Iran war continues.

diplomatic_visits.title: Defining global leadership in AI at Trump-Xi summit
diplomatic_visits.description: Former U.S. deputy national security advisor Anne Neuberger is watching for signs of competition and cooperation on artificial intelligence at President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping's summit this week.

elections.title: Morocco holds elections after mass migration attempts and deadly youth protests. Here's what to know
elections.description: Moroccan voters are heading to the polls to elect a new parliament, with a focus on jobs, wages, and inequality

elections.title: Russians abroad voted eight to one against Putin's party, defying official results
elections.description: Two independent exit polls covering 27 countries put New People first with around 45% and United Russia as low as 2.8%, the reverse of official results inside Russia, where Putin's party took nearly 58%. Exit poll organisers said the gap "destroys the image of supposed support for the authorities."

elections.title: Who actually has power at the United Nations?
elections.description: Every country at the UN gets a vote. But five countries have a power the other 188 don’t: the power of veto in the UNSC.

elections.title: 'No surprises' as results emerge in Russian parliamentary election
elections.description: Preliminary results suggest that Kremlin-backed United Russia is on course to retain its constitutional majority.

elections.title: Ethiopia's main armed groups form anti-government alliance
elections.description: In tonight's edition: A coalition of opposition groups band together in the hope of ousting Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. Also, we speak to the deputy chief of the UN's peacekeeping mission in DR Congo. And with just a few days to go before legislative elections, young Moroccans are torn between hope and scepticism ahead of the crucial vote.
